title: hops[int(off)] is dereferenced after non-fatal ok/count expectf checks — a count-0 regression mis-reads the first packed hop row instead of failing via the pinned message
evidence:
off, count, ok := routing_equal_cost_hops(&s.routing, &s.topology, res, host)
testing.expectf(t, ok, "(res,host) must resolve")
testing.expectf(t, count == 1,
	"the re-priced fat bundle must win UNIQUELY (count 1), got %d", count)
testing.expectf(t, s.routing.hops[int(off)].node == m1,
	"next hop must be m1 (bundle priced at its min member: 5+5=10), got %d — the bundle edge was NOT re-priced",
	s.routing.hops[int(off)].node)
detail: routing_equal_cost_hops returns (0, 0, false) when the table is stale and hop_offset defaults to 0 for unroutable pairs, so a route-vanishing regression yields count 0, off 0, and hops[0] reads an unrelated pair's row (or panics if hops is empty).
recommended_fix: Guard the hops dereferences with `if ok && count == 1` so the expectf message is the failure, matching the r1 W1 pattern.

title: pipe_tier[rep_slot] / pipe_id[rep_slot] dereferenced after a non-fatal rep_slot != -1 check — a bundle with no live member indexes -1 and panics
evidence:
testing.expectf(t, rep_slot != -1, "the res-m1 bundle must have a live member")
testing.expectf(t, s.topology.pipe_tier[rep_slot] == narrow,
	"the lowest-slot member is the FIRST-DRAWN narrow pipe, got tier %d want %d",
	s.topology.pipe_tier[rep_slot], narrow)
testing.expectf(t, s.routing.hops[int(off)].pipe == s.topology.pipe_id[rep_slot],
	"representative Hop.pipe must stay the LOWEST-SLOT member (pipe %d, tier narrow), got %d",
	s.topology.pipe_id[rep_slot], s.routing.hops[int(off)].pipe)
detail: expectf records and continues; if the bundle has no live member rep_slot stays -1 and pipe_tier[-1] / pipe_id[-1] are negative slice indices — an out-of-bounds panic instead of the pinned failure message.
recommended_fix: Guard the tier/pipe asserts with `if rep_slot != -1` so the rep_slot expectf message is the failure.
